text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Australian poet LESBIA HARFORD was born in 1891.
American actor and singer PAUL ROBESON was born in 1898.
Australian ballet legend SIR ROBERT HELPMANN was born in 1909.
American publisher of 'Playboy' magazine, HUGH HEFNER, was born in 1926.
One of Australia's most respected actors RON HADDRICK, who played Sheffield Shield cricket for South Australia in 1952, was born in 1929.
American pioneering rock 'n' roller CARL PERKINS, who wrote "Blue Suede Shoes", was born in 1932.
UK leadsinger and drummer with 'Paper Lace', PHILIP WRIGHT, was born in 1948. Hits included "Billy Don't Be A Hero" (1974) and "The Night Chicago Died" (1974).
Australian television presenter/host JANA WENDT was born in 1957.
Australian singer JAMIE REDFERN, who began his career with 'Young Talent Time' before being launched internationally by LIBERACE, was born in 1957.
Spanish golfer SEVERIANO BALLESTEROS was born in 1957.
** EVENTS **
1626 : British philosopher and statesman SIR FRANCIS
BACON ("Essays") died.
1865 : The Confederate Army of North Virginia under
General ROBERT E. LEE surrendered to the Union Army's General ULYSSES S. GRANT at the Appomattox Courthouse in Virginia.
1940 : Germany invaded Norway and Denmark.
1945 : German theologian DIETRICH BONHOEFFER, who
involved himself with anti-HITLER conspirators, died in Buchenwald concentration camp.
1959 : American architect FRANK LLOYD WRIGHT died. He
once said "The physician can bury his mistakes, but the architect can only advise his clients to plant vines!"
1960 : DAVID PRATT fired two shots at South African
President DR HENDRIK VERWOERD in an assassination attempt, succeeding only in wounding him.
1962 : Australian Prime Minister BOB MENZIES opened the
coaxial cable linking Sydney-Canberra-Melbourne by phone.
1963 : The film "Lawrence Of Arabia" starring PETER
O'TOOLE won 7 Oscars including Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Score.
1966 : Film producer CARLO PONTI married actress SOPHIA
LOREN in Paris, even though according to Italian law he was still married to his previous wife.
1970 : PAUL MCCARTNEY issued a High Court writ winding-up
the business partnership of THE BEATLES. The move was no surprise, as MCCARTNEY had been upset with Apple Records and had fought with other band members over money for several months.
1981 : "Nature" magazine published a paper containing the
longest ever scientific word of 207-thousand letters!
1989 : Namibia moved closer towards independence with the
announcement of a ceasefire between South Africa's armed forces and guerilla fighters of the South West Africa People's Organisation (SWAPO).
1994 : Japanese Prime Minister MORIHIRO HOSAKAWA stood
down over allegations of financial impropriety.
1994 : British police identified the ninth body, found at
the so-called "House of Horrors" in Gloucester. Fifty-two year-old FREDERICK WEST killed himself before facing trial for mass murder.
